summary: The Customers page plots every NovaBank customer as a dot on a 0-100 risk spectrum and lists them in a table sorted by risk, with an instant text filter. Everything comes from one `GET /users` call: filtering runs in the browser, and clicking a dot or a row opens the customer drawer from `views/details.js`. The page has no live subscriptions or timers, so its `render` doesn't take the cleanup context.

notes.text: Header comment: a risk spectrum (each customer as a dot on the 0-100 scale) and a table that is sorted by risk and can be filtered by name, ID or city.
The `get` API helper and DOM helpers. `esc` is imported because the tooltip content is a plain string rather than an `html` template, so values must be escaped by hand.
Motion helpers, plus the avatar, panel and score-bar fragments.
`icon`, the shared pointer-following tooltip (`showTip` and `hideTip`) and the customer drawer.
`row` renders one customer row. `data-user` makes the whole row open the drawer; the first cell shows the initials avatar, name and ID.
Segment, home city, current risk as a coloured score bar, and the total number of events.
Open incidents in red when there are any (a faint `0` otherwise), followed by the total incident count, so the cell reads like `2 / 5`.
How long ago the customer was last active, then the end of the row.
Page module titled `Customers`. `render` only takes `view`, because the page has nothing to clean up: no live subscriptions and no intervals.
Fetches every customer and sorts the riskiest first, breaking ties by ID so the order stays stable between visits.
Counts **elevated** customers: those with a current score of 60 or more, which means HIGH or CRITICAL.
Mounts the page markup.

Header. The description defines current risk the same way the backend's `users_overview` computes it: the highest score among the customer's ten most recent events, so one bad session stays visible for a while. Tags show the customer count and, in orange, how many are elevated.
Full-width **Risk spectrum** panel with a usage hint, and the inner container (`data-spectrum`) that the dots are added to.
Background zones sized 30/30/20/20% so their edges fall exactly on the engine's thresholds (30, 60 and 80), plus axis labels positioned by percentage. The last line closes the panel and its grid row.
**All customers** panel, with the filter input in its header.
The table: a header row plus a `data-rows` body containing every customer, already sorted by risk.
Building the spectrum. `stacks` counts how many dots each score bucket already holds, so customers with the same score pile up instead of covering each other.

For each customer the bucket is `round(score / 3)`; engine scores are always multiples of 5, so in practice each bucket holds exactly one score. `n` is the customer's zero-based position in the bucket (increment the count, then subtract one).

Adds a dot button coloured by level. It sits at `score%` from the left, shifted 15 px right for every completed stack of five, and rises 15 px per position within its stack; the `aria-label` gives screen readers the name and score.
Pops every dot in from zero size with a springy overshoot (`outBack`), 25 ms apart, so the distribution visibly builds up.
One delegated `pointermove` listener on the spectrum. When the pointer isn't over a dot it hides the tooltip; the `return` just exits early.
Looks up the hovered customer and shows a tooltip with ID, name, score and level, and home city. Every value goes through `esc` because `showTip` sets `innerHTML`.
Hides the tooltip when the pointer leaves the spectrum.
Fades the table rows up, 22 ms apart, capped at 25 rows so the animation stays short.
The filter box listens for `input`, which fires on every keystroke and paste.
Lowercases the query and re-renders the table body with the customers whose name, ID or home city contain it. All customers are already in memory, so filtering needs no request and no debounce.
One delegated click listener: dots and rows both carry `data-user`, so either one opens the customer drawer.
Closes `render` and the page object.
